title: Thunder vs. Lakers Post-Game Stats: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Leads OKC's 121-92 Rout Of LA - NewsBreak
text:
By Tanishq Sharma ,
42 minutes ago
Austin Reaves, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Marcus Smart (Photo by Imagn Images) The defending champions, the Oklahoma City Thunder, absolutely dominated the Los Angeles Lakers in their first matchup of the 2025-26 NBA season. Reigning NBA MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who recently revealed why he didn’t enjoy their championship win , led the OKC to clinch their fourth consecutive victory as the Thunder vs. Lakers game ended 121-92.
The OKC Thunder took control from the first quarter, leading the Lakers by 12 points. The home side extended its lead to 32 points at the end of the first half. With a score of 70-38, the Lakers registered the fewest points in the first half since 2021.
In the first half, the Lakers struggled big time with their superstars, Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, combining for more turnovers than made field goals. Doncic and Reaves made six field goals in 20 attempts and had seven turnovers combined. The Lakers had 11 turnovers while the Thunder had just one in the first half. Overall, the Lakers had 20 turnovers as compared to OKC’s 11.
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Scores 30 As Lakers Stars Struggle Against OKC Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Alex Caruso (Photo by Imagn Images) While Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the game in scoring with his 30 points in 29 minutes, the Thunder played a spectacular two-way game led by Alex Caruso and Chet Holmgren. The two-time NBA champion, Caruso, registered 10 points, four rebounds, three assists, and two steals in just 16 minutes.
On the other hand, Holmgren played 20 minutes, scoring 11 points and blocking two shots. Seven Thunder players scored in double digits, including SGA, Caruso, Holmgren, Ajay Mitchell (14), Isaisah Hartenstein (11), Isaiah Joe (21), and Ousmane Dieng (10).
Meanwhile, the Lakers had a rough night, showing struggles to score against the Thunder. Doncic led the Lakers with 19 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, and two steals. He shot just 1-of-7 from three. Dalton Knecht had 16 points in 19 minutes with 4-of-5 field goals from beyond the arc.
Austin Revaes went 0-of-5 from three and ended up with 13 points, five rebounds, and three assists. Rui Hachimura also had an off day from the long range, and he finished the game with 13 points. With this loss, the Lakers drop to an 8-4 record while the Thunder improved to 12-1.
